title: C language standards: historical versions and selecting a target standard
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its relevant rules.
Trace the example and justify its behaviour.
Identify important assumptions and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a reviewed and tested exercise.

understand.concept: C has evolved through standardized revisions including C90, C99, C11, C17 and C23. A project should select a target standard based on compiler support, platform requirements and needed language/library features, then use consistent build settings.
understand.whyItMatters: Standards selection affects syntax, library availability, diagnostics and portability. Explicit targets reduce accidental dependence on compiler defaults.
understand.analogy: Treat standards, interfaces and release steps as explicit contracts that make assumptions visible.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, implementation documentation or project-specific requirements.

explain.narrative:
C has evolved through standardized revisions including C90, C99, C11, C17 and C23. A project should select a target standard based on compiler support, platform requirements and needed language/library features, then use consistent build settings.

State assumptions and constraints, consult the applicable standard or tool documentation, and verify the result with appropriate compiler diagnostics and tests. Separate portable guarantees from implementation-specific behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The command selects C17 on a GCC/Clang-like toolchain. Other compilers may use different options and have different support levels.

practise.guidedTask: List reasons a project might target C17 rather than a newer standard.
practise.independentTask: Choose a target standard for a legacy embedded project and justify the decision using compiler support and required features.
hints: Do not assume every compiler implements every recent standard feature fully.
